+If your computer can’t communicate with our software update servers, you might see one of these messages.
+If you see one of these messages, make sure that your Mac is up to date.
-- This device isn't eligible for the requested build.
+- Error: This device isn't eligible for the requested build.
-If you see one of these messages and need help updating or restoring your iOS or iPadOS device, make sure your Mac is up to date.

-If you're using iTunes, [install the latest version of iTunes](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) and try to update or restore your device again. If you're using Apple Devices on your PC, make sure you [use the latest version](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118406) . If you still can't update or restore, follow the steps below.

+If you're using iTunes, [install the latest version of iTunes](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) and update or restore your device again. If you're using the Apple Devices app on your PC, make sure that you [update to the latest version](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118406) .
-If you have a firewall or security software installed on your computer, they might block access to some Apple software update servers. Try these steps:
+A firewall or security software installed on your computer might block access to our software update servers.

-- [Be sure you have a working Internet connection](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101181) . Try visiting [www.apple.com](https://www.apple.com/) or contact your Internet service provider for more help.
+- [Check your Internet connection](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101588) . [Visit our website](http://www.apple.com) or contact your internet service provider (ISP) for more help.
-- Make sure that your security software or firewall allows access to [Apple software update servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101555#firewalls) .
+- Make sure that your firewall allows [access to our update servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101555#firewalls) .
-- [Configure or temporarily uninstall](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111760) your security software.
+- [Set up or temporarily uninstall](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111760) your security software.
-- Bypass your Internet router. Some routers might block iTunes from accessing the update server. Try the following:
+- Bypass your Internet router. Some routers might block iTunes from accessing the update server.
-- Disconnect from your wired or wireless router and use an Ethernet cable to connect your computer directly to your modem.
+- Disconnect from your wired or wireless router.
-- Restart your computer and modem. Contact your Internet service provider for instructions on using your modem.
+- Connect your computer to your modem using an Ethernet cable.
-After you confirm your Internet connection is working, try to [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.
+- Restart your computer and modem.
+- Contact your ISP for instructions on using your modem.
+After you confirm your Internet connection is working, [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.

-Try to restore or update on another computer with a different Internet connection. Trying this helps to make sure there aren't issues with your computer that might stop it from communicating with the update server.
+Restore or update on another computer with a different Internet connection. This helps you rule out issues with your computer that might block communication with the update server.

-Errors 1639, 3000-3020, and 3100-3999 (with the exception of 3194) are sometimes caused by your network settings. If your computer uses a managed network, contact your network administrator. Proxies, firewalls, and other network security measures can cause these errors. If necessary, find a different network connection to restore the device. For example, if you're restoring at work, try to restore at home or on a friend's computer and network.

+Your network settings sometimes cause errors 1639, 3000-3020, and 3100-3999 (except 3194). If your computer uses a managed network, contact your network administrator. Proxies, firewalls, and other network security measures can cause these errors.
+If necessary, find a different network connection to restore the device. For example, if you're restoring at work, restore at home or on a friend's computer and network.
-After you update your Mac or update iTunes or Apple Devices to the latest version, check the hosts file to make sure your computer can contact the update server.
+- Update your Mac, iTunes, or Apple Devices app.
+- Check the hosts file to make sure that your computer can contact the update server.

-If you’re using a Windows computer, see the steps from the [Microsoft support site](http://support.microsoft.com/kb/972034) . Resetting the hosts file affects software services that rely on hosts file redirects. If you're using Windows on a business computer, ensure applications work correctly after you reset your hosts file.

+If you're using a Windows computer, see [How to reset the Hosts file back to the default](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/how-to-reset-the-hosts-file-back-to-the-default) on the Microsoft support site. Resetting the hosts file might affect other software on your computer. If you're using a business computer, check that your apps work correctly after you reset the hosts file.
-### Check your host files on macOS
+### Check your hosts file on macOS
-[Image: An image of a terminal window]
+[Image: Terminal window showing the hosts file with the gs.apple.com entry commented out.]
-6. Add the # symbol and a space ("# ") to the beginning of the gs.apple.com entry.
+6. Add a '# ' before the gs.apple.com entry.
-After your computer finishes restarting, try to [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.
+After your computer finishes restarting, [update](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) or [restore](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118107) your iOS or iPadOS device again.

-## Share feedback to help improve Apple Intelligence
+## Share feedback to help improve Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

-Apple Intelligence — the personal intelligence system built into iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro — combines Apple-built models with your personal context to deliver intelligence that is most useful and relevant, all while protecting your privacy. +Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are designed to protect your privacy at every step, while making responses and conversations more contextual and helpful.

+- Apple also collects your device model, operating system version, language, and the version of the Apple Intelligence model that is relevant to your feedback.

description: If you see Error 53 while updating or restoring, find steps to fix it.
diff_excerpt: -If you see Error 53 on your computer, learn what to do.
+If you see Error 53 while updating or restoring, find steps to fix it.
-If you try to update or restore your iPhone or iPad with macOS Catalina 10.15 or later in Finder, macOS Mojave 10.14 or earlier, or a PC with iTunes, you might see Error 53 on your computer.

+When updating or restoring your iPhone or iPad, you might see Error 53. This can happen in Finder with macOS Catalina 10.15 or later. It can also happen with macOS Mojave 10.14 or earlier, or with iTunes on a PC.

-For anyone who experienced Error 53 before February 2016, Apple released an update in iOS 9.3 to allow you to restore your device using your Mac or PC. Use the steps in this article to restore and recover your device.
+If you saw Error 53 before February 2016, you can fix it now. In iOS 9.3, Apple released an update that lets you restore your device using your Mac or PC.

-- Make sure that your [Mac has the latest software updates](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108382) . If you're using iTunes, make sure that your device has the [latest version of iTunes](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) .
+- Make sure that [your Mac has the latest software updates](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108382) .
+- If you use iTunes, [update it to the latest version](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118290) .
-- When you see the option to Restore or Update, click Update. Your computer will try to reinstall the software and restore your device without erasing your data. 1
+- When you see Restore or Update, click Update to reinstall the software without erasing your data.
-- If you can't get past the Apple logo screen, force restart 2 your device. When you see the option to Restore or Update, click Restore.
+- If you can't get past the Apple logo, [force restart your device](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/force-restart-iphone-iph8903c3ee6/ios) , then click Restore.
-- When you see your device's Hello screen, follow the onscreen steps to set up your device.
+- When you see the Hello screen, follow the onscreen setup steps.
-- If you previously backed up your device, you can [set up from your backup](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118105) .
+- If you previously backed up your device, [set up from your backup](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118105) .
-- When you see the screen for Touch ID, tap Set up Touch ID later.
+- When you see the Touch ID screen, tap Set Up Touch ID Later.
-If you see Error 53 when installing iOS 9.3 or later, [make sure your computer can communicate with Apple’s servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108396) , or try another computer.
+If you see Error 53 when installing iOS 9.3 or later, make sure that your computer can [communicate with Apple's servers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108396) . If it can't, try another computer.

-If Touch ID on your device didn't work before you saw Error 53, the feature still won't work after you update or restore your device and you might need service. [Get service](https://getsupport.apple.com/?caller=ikb)
+If Touch ID didn't work before you saw Error 53, it still won't work after you restore your device. [You might need service](https://getsupport.apple.com/?caller=ikb) .
-- If the restore won't finish and you see an error code other than Error 53, [learn what to do](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108308) .
+## Learn more
-- To force restart your device, press and hold both the Sleep/Wake and Home or Side buttons until you see the Apple logo again.
+- [Fix other restore errors.](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108308)

-## Use the App Store
+## Use Terminal
+You can use Terminal to download the installer for compatible macOS versions no earlier than the version that came with your Mac, or the closest version still available.
+- Make sure that your Mac is using macOS Catalina 10.15 or later.
+- Open Terminal, which is in the Utilities folder of the Applications folder. Or Use Spotlight or Siri AI in the menu bar to find and open Terminal.

+- Type or paste this command in Terminal, replacing "[number]" with the [latest macOS version number](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109033#latest) for the compatible macOS that you want to download: softwareupdate --fetch-full-installer --full-installer-version [number]
+- Example: softwareupdate --fetch-full-installer --full-installer-version 26.6.2
+- Press Return to enter the command.
+- As macOS downloads to the Applications folder, Terminal shows the percentage it’s installing (downloading).

+- If Terminal says update not found, that version of macOS is not available for your Mac. You can enter softwareupdate --list-full-installers to get a list of macOS versions that are currently available for your Mac model.

+- When Terminal says that the install finished successfully, the download is complete. Open the Applications folder and double-click the macOS installer, named Install [Version Name], then follow the onscreen installation instructions. Or leave the installer in the Applications folder for later use.

+A bootable installer can be useful when you want to install macOS on multiple computers without downloading the installer each time, or when you can't install using other methods.

diff_excerpt: -# Sign out of iCloud on your devices
+# Sign out of your Apple Account and iCloud on your devices
-If you want to stop using iCloud on one of your devices, learn how to sign out and what happens when you sign out.
+If you want to stop using iCloud and other Apple services on one of your devices, learn how to sign out and what happens when you sign out.
+## Before you sign out

+When you sign out of Apple Account on your device, you're automatically signed out of iCloud, the App Store and other Apple media services, iMessage, and FaceTime. Any information stored in iCloud remains available in iCloud. Your iCloud data will be removed from your device unless you choose to keep a copy of that data when prompted. To help prevent data loss:
+- Make sure that you have an up-to-date [iCloud backup](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108366) .
+- If you recently made changes to content synced with iCloud, wait before signing out, or check [iCloud.com](https://www.icloud.com) or another device to make sure that your changes have synced.
+- Not everything is backed up in iCloud — make sure you have access to anything [not synced to iCloud](https://support.apple.com/en-us/104958#signouticloud) .
+- Apple recommends, in addition to an iCloud backup, that you also [archive or make copies of the information that you store in iCloud](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108306) .
+- If you don’t know your Apple Account password, [change your password](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101567) before you sign out of a trusted device.
+## Sign out on your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Vision Pro
+- Open the Settings app, then tap [your name].
+- Scroll down to the bottom. Tap Sign Out.
+- Choose Erase this [Device] or [Sign Out But Don't Erase](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122682) .
+- Follow the onscreen prompts to learn what information will remain on your device or be erased.

To ease this transition, Apple created Rosetta, which works in the background to automatically translate Intel-based apps for use with Apple silicon. -Rosetta is currently available for any Mac with Apple silicon, and it will remain available through the forthcoming macOS 27 — the next major macOS release. -For optimal performance and future compatibility, you should update your Intel-based apps, plug-ins, extensions, and other add-ons for Apple silicon.
+## Identify Intel-based apps
+To learn which of your apps need to be updated for Apple silicon, use the Finder or System Settings.
+### Use the Finder
+- Locate the app in the Finder. Most apps are in the Applications folder, which you can access from the sidebar of any Finder window.
+- Click the app once to select it.
+- From the File menu in the Finder menu bar, choose Get Info. Or press Command-I.
+- In the Info window that opens, find the information shown after Kind:
+- Application (Intel): The app is made for a Mac with an Intel processor. You should update the app for Apple silicon.
+- Application (Universal): The app is made for both a Mac with Apple silicon and a Mac with an Intel processor.
+- Application (Apple silicon): The app is made for a Mac with Apple silicon.
+[Image: Info window for an Intel-based app.]

+For Universal apps, app developers can include an "Open using Rosetta" setting in the Info window. If this setting is available for your app, you can use it in macOS 27 or earlier to force the app to open as an Intel-based app, which allows it to use Intel-only plug-ins, extensions, and other add-ons. If you later update the add-on for Apple silicon, deselect this setting.
+### Use System Settings
+- Make sure that you’re using macOS 27 or later.
+- From the Apple menu , choose System Settings.
+- Click General in the sidebar, then click About on the right.
+- In the macOS section, click the Details button next to Intel-based Apps.
+[Image: Intel-based Apps section in the General pane of System Settings.]

+- A list of Intel-based apps appears, showing apps that you recently used or that are installed in common locations. To show an app in the Finder or move it to the Trash, move your pointer over the app’s name, click the More Info button , then choose Show App in Finder or Move to Trash.
+[Image: List of Intel-based apps in System Settings.]

description: Learn about lossless audio in Apple Music and how to turn it on or off for your device.
diff_excerpt: -## What is lossless audio compression?
-Most audio compression techniques lose some amount of data contained in the original source file. Lossless compression is a form of compression that preserves all of the original data.

-Apple has developed its own lossless audio compression technology called Apple Lossless Audio Codec (ALAC). In addition to AAC, most of the Apple Music catalog is now also encoded using ALAC in resolutions ranging from 16-bit/44.1 kHz (CD Quality) up to 24-bit/192 kHz.

-While the difference between AAC and lossless audio is virtually indistinguishable, we’re offering Apple Music subscribers the option to access most of the Music catalog in lossless audio compression.
+With an Apple Music subscription, you can turn on lossless audio across all of your devices and hear every preserved detail from the original recording.
-- Go to Settings > Apps.
+- Go to Settings.
+- Tap Apps.
-- Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/48 kHz
-- Hi-Res Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/192 kHz
-- In the menu bar, choose Music > Preferences.
+- In the menu bar, choose Music, then select Preferences.
-- Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/48 kHz
-- Hi-Res Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/192 kHz
+- Tap the More button .
-- Go to Settings > Apps.
+- Go to Settings.
+- Select Apps.
-- Select Audio Quality.
-- Select or unselect Lossless. Apple TV 4K currently doesn’t support Hi-Res Lossless (sample rates greater than 48 kHz).
+- Select Audio Quality. From here, you can choose the audio quality for streaming audio.
-- AirPods 4, AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 with USB-C Charging Case, or Powerbeats Pro 2
+- AirPods 4 or later, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 with USB-C Charging Case, or Powerbeats Pro 2
-- Go to Settings > Apps.
+- Go to Settings.
+- Tap Apps.
+## About lossless audio with Apple and Beats headphones

+AirPods 3 or earlier, AirPods Pro 1, AirPods Pro 2 with Lightning Charging Case, AirPods Max, and most Beats wireless headphones use Apple AAC Bluetooth Codec to ensure excellent audio quality. However, Bluetooth connections aren't lossless.

+You can listen to lossless audio with AirPods Max 1 (USB-C) and AirPods Max 2 . Update your iPhone, iPad, or Mac to the most recent software version, and update your AirPods Max to the most recent firmware version. Use the included USB-C to USB-C cable to connect your AirPods Max to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac with a USB-C port. Or, use a USB-C to USB-A cable to connect your AirPods Max to a Mac with a USB-A port.
-- Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/48 kHz
-- Hi-Res Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/192 kHz
-- Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/48 kHz
-- Hi-Res Lossless for a maximum resolution of 24-bit/192 kHz
-## Frequently asked questions about lossless
-### Can I listen to lossless audio using AirPods, AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, or Beats headphones?

-AirPods 3 or earlier, AirPods Pro 1, AirPods Pro 2 with Lightning Charging Case, AirPods Max, and most Beats wireless headphones use Apple AAC Bluetooth Codec to ensure excellent audio quality. However, Bluetooth connections aren't lossless.

-AirPods 4, AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 with USB-C Charging Case, and Powerbeats Pro 2 use a proprietary wireless audio protocol that can provide Lossless Audio with ultra-low latency when paired with Apple Vision Pro.

-You can listen to lossless audio with AirPods Max 1 (USB-C) and AirPods Max 2 . Update your iPhone, iPad, or Mac to the most recent software version, and update your AirPods Max to the most recent firmware version. Use the included USB-C to USB-C cable to connect your AirPods Max to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac with a USB-C port. Or, use a USB-C to USB-A cable to connect your AirPods Max to a Mac with a USB-A port.
-### Can I listen to lossless audio over Bluetooth?
-Lossless will play back normally on Bluetooth speakers and headphones. However, Bluetooth connections don’t support lossless audio.
-### Can I listen to lossless audio using Apple’s Lightning to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter?

-Yes. The Lightning to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter is designed to transmit audio from the iPhone’s Lightning connector. It contains a digital-to-analog converter that supports up to 24-bit/48 kHz lossless audio.
-### Can I listen to lossless audio using the AirPods Max Lightning to 3.5mm Audio Cable or USB-C to 3.5 mm Audio Cable?

-The Lightning to 3.5 mm Audio Cable and [USB-C to 3.5 mm Audio Cable](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/MDV84AM/A/usb-c-to-35-mm-audio-cable-12-m) are designed to allow AirPods Max to connect to analog sources. AirPods Max can be connected to devices playing Lossless and Hi-Res Lossless recordings with exceptional audio quality. However, given the analog-to-digital conversion in the cable, the playback will not be completely lossless.
-### What content isn’t available in lossless audio?
-- Broadcast radio
-- Live radio and on-demand content from Apple Music 1, Apple Music Hits, and Apple Music Country
title: About lossless audio in Apple Music

description: You can cancel the AppleCare plan or policy coverage for your devices, whether you pay monthly or annually, or paid upfront in full for your plan.
diff_excerpt: -# Cancel your AppleCare plan coverage
+# Cancel AppleCare coverage for your Apple device
-Learn how to cancel the AppleCare coverage for your Apple product.
+You can cancel the AppleCare plan or policy coverage for your devices, whether you pay monthly or annually, or paid upfront in full for your plan.

If you cancel AppleCare coverage for your device, you might be able to [get new AppleCare coverage](https://support.apple.com/104941) later if you change your mind.

+If you don't want to keep AppleCare coverage for your Apple device, you can cancel your plan or policy based on how you purchased the coverage. 1 If you cancel AppleCare coverage for your device, you might be able to [get new AppleCare coverage](https://support.apple.com/104941) later if you change your mind.

-If your AppleCare+ plan was canceled after upgrading to an AppleCare One plan, you will receive a refund based on the percentage of unexpired AppleCare plan coverage. If the original plan was paid upfront in full, this may be sent as an Apple Gift Card.

-You can find more information about canceling your plan and refund expectations in [the applicable AppleCare Terms and Conditions](https://www.apple.com/legal/sales-support/) for your country or region.
+If you purchased recurring AppleCare coverage from a wireless carrier or other reseller, contact the carrier or reseller to request a refund.
-If you purchased recurring AppleCare coverage from a wireless carrier or other reseller, contact the carrier or reseller to request a refund.

description: Screen Time comes with parental controls that can help you manage the apps and websites your child can access, who they communicate with, when they use their devices, and more.
diff_excerpt: -# Use parental controls to manage your child's iPhone or iPad
-With Screen Time, there are a number of settings and parental controls that you can use to help keep your child's device usage safe, private, and age appropriate.
-## What you can do with parental controls

-Apple's parental controls are important tools that allow parents and guardians to choose how — and how often — their children use their devices. Parental controls are built directly into iPhone, iPad, and Mac, and can help you manage the downloads and purchases your child can make, who they can communicate with, and the apps and other content they can access.

-Before you can set parental controls for a child's device, you need to [set up Family Sharing on your device](https://setup.iCloud.com/family/messages?aaaction=showFamilyInvite&inviteCode=organizer_create&campaign=kbArticle) . Then add your child's Apple Account to your family group.

-When Family Sharing is set up, and your child's Apple Account is added to the Family Sharing group, you need to [turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#set-restrictions) . Then you're ready to start setting and managing parental controls. Depending on your country or region, and your child's age, some parental controls are on by default. *

-You can use some Screen Time features without turning on Content & Privacy Restrictions or setting parental controls. For example, you can enable Screen Distance to help reduce eye strain; Communication Limits to manage how your child communicates with others; and Communication Safety to help detect inappropriate photos and videos before they're even sent from or viewed on your child's device. [Learn more about Screen Time](https://support.apple.com/108806) .
-* Age varies by country or region. [Learn more about settings and features for kids by country or region](https://support.apple.com/125666) .
-## Turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions

-When you set up Screen Time on your child's device, you can set age-related restrictions for content, purchases and downloads, privacy settings, and more. If you chose to set it up later, you can turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions in Screen Time.
-- Open the Settings app, scroll down, then tap Screen Time.
-- Under Family, tap your child's name.
-- Tap Content & Privacy Restrictions. If asked, enter your Screen Time passcode, then turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions.
-If you turn off Content & Privacy Restrictions, the parental controls that you set within Content & Privacy Restrictions will pause until you turn it on again.
-## Set and manage parental controls for your child's device

-In order for the parental control settings to sync across all the devices in your Family Sharing group, make sure that all devices have the latest software version before you turn on parental controls or change any of the parental controls settings. Some parental controls are turned on by default depending on the child's age. Here's what you can manage for your child's device.
-- [Prevent App Store purchases](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#prevent-purchases)
-- [Allow built-in apps and features](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#allow-apps)
-- [Prevent explicit content and manage content ratings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#explicit-content)
-- [Prevent inappropriate web content](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#web-content)
-- [Restrict Game Center features](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#restrict-games)
-- [Restrict Intelligence & Siri features](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#restrict-siri)
-- [Prevent changes to privacy settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#privacy-settings)
-- [Prevent or allow changes to other settings and features](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#allow-changes)
-- [Make changes to health and safety features](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#other)
-- [If you can't respond to your child's exception request](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105121#requests)
-### Prevent App Store purchases
-You can prevent your child from being able to install or delete apps, make in-app purchases in apps installed from the App Store, and more.
-- Open the Settings app, scroll down, then tap Screen Time.
-- Under Family, tap your child's name.
+# Set up parental controls to manage your child's iPhone or iPad
+Screen Time comes with parental controls that can help you manage the apps and websites your child can access, who they communicate with, when they use their devices, and more.

+In iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27, Screen Time introduces new parental controls to help parents manage what kids access, when they use devices, and how they stay safe while communicating with others. To access these updated parental controls, make sure every device in your Family Sharing group is using these software versions. The Family Sharing organizer or a parent/guardian also needs to update the parental controls for the family group.

+If you can't update every device in your Family Sharing group, you can continue to use the previous version of Screen Time and parental controls, or adjust the parental controls directly on the child's device.
+## Before you get started
+- [Make sure you have Family Sharing set up](https://setup.icloud.com/family/messages?aaaction=showFamilyInvite&inviteCode=organizer_create&campaign=kbArticle) .

+- [Create a Child Account for your child](https://support.apple.com/102617) , if they don't have one already. Then make sure your child's Apple Account is part of your Family Sharing group. It's important that your child has their own Apple Account, and isn't sharing an account with anyone else (for example, another family member).

+- Update all devices in your Family Sharing group to iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and/or visionOS 27, then [update your parental controls](https://support.apple.com/guide/child-safety/jrzvk3ml3unm) to access the new Screen Time and parental controls experience.
+- Make sure the Family Sharing organizer or another parent/guardian is added to the child's contacts list so the child's requests can be sent for approval.

+Not all parental controls are available on all Apple devices. Some parental controls are located within Screen Time, and some are enabled through the settings directly — like Apple TV on the web. Depending on your state, country, or region, and your child's age, some parental controls are on by default and can't be removed. 1

description: A recovery key is an optional security feature that helps improve the security of your Apple Account. If you forgot your Apple Account password, your recovery key can help you regain access to your account.
diff_excerpt: -A recovery key is an optional security feature that helps improve the security of your Apple Account. If you lose access to your account, you can use your recovery key to reset your password and regain access.

+A recovery key is an optional security feature that helps improve the security of your Apple Account. If you forgot your Apple Account password, your recovery key can help you regain access to your account.
-## Improve your Apple Account security with a recovery key
+## What’s a recovery key?
-A recovery key is a secret 28-character code that you can use, along with a trusted phone number and an Apple device, to recover your account and data.
+If you set up a recovery key and can’t provide it when you lose access to your account, you’ll be locked out of your account permanently.
-- When you set up a recovery key, you turn off Apple’s standard [account recovery process](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118574) .

+A recovery key is a 28-character code that you can use, along with a trusted phone number and an Apple device, to help you regain access to your Apple Account. If you use [Advanced Data Protection for iCloud](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108756) , a recovery key can also help you access your end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. This feature is optional.
-- Instead, access to a trusted device or your recovery key is required to reset your Apple Account password and sign in to your account if you ever lose access.
+When you set up a recovery key, you turn off Apple’s standard [account recovery process](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118574) .
-This gives you more control of your account recovery methods and can help prevent an attacker from gaining access to and taking control of your account.
+- Instead, you must use your recovery key and your trusted phone number to reset your Apple Account password.

-If you don't know your account password and have lost or otherwise don't have a trusted device, you need your recovery key to regain access to your Apple Account. If you can't provide your recovery key, you’ll be locked out of your account permanently.
+- You should print a copy of your recovery key or write it down . If you lose it, Apple can’t provide you with your recovery key.

-Print a copy of your recovery key or write it down. Keep your key in a safe place, and consider storing a copy in more than one place. You can also give a copy of your recovery key to a trusted family member.
+- Without your recovery key, you might lose access to all your Apple Account data.
-Don’t store your recovery key in your Apple Passwords app, iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive. If you lose access to your Apple Account, you won’t be able to open these apps to find it.

+This gives you more control of your account recovery methods and can help prevent an attacker from gaining access to and taking control of your account. Additionally, when you change certain information about your Apple Account, you might be asked for your recovery key. For example, if you add a new trusted phone number, you’ll be asked for your recovery key.
-## What you need

+Keep a copy of your key in a safe place, and consider storing it in more than one place. Don’t store your recovery key in your Apple Passwords app, iCloud Photos, Notes, or iCloud Drive. If you lose access to your Apple Account, you won’t be able to open these apps to find it.
-Before you set up a recovery key:

-## Recovery key and Advanced Data Protection for iCloud

+# Manage your child's access to apps and app requests on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

-With Ask to Buy turned on, your child can request to download an app with an age rating higher than the app's age-rating restriction you set for them in Screen Time. If you approve an exception, you can remove it later.

+Screen Time comes with parental controls — like Ask to Buy — which requires your child to request access to apps they want to download. You also get a notification whenever your child tries to download an app rated above the age rating that you've set for them. Each approved app gets added to an allowed list, which you can adjust at any time.
-## How app exception requests work

+In iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27, Screen Time introduces new parental controls to help parents manage what kids access, when they use their devices, and how they stay safe while communicating with others. To access these updated parental controls, make sure every device in your Family Sharing group is using these software versions. The Family Sharing organizer or a parent/guardian also needs to update the parental controls for the family group.

-If your child tries to download an app with an age rating higher than the app age-rating restriction that you set for them, they see a message that says content restrictions are enabled. If they ask for an exception, you'll receive a message in the Messages app. You can approve or decline the request right from the message notification or in the Messages app.
+If you can't update every device in your Family Sharing group, you can continue to use the previous version of Screen Time and parental controls.

-[Depending on your state, country, or region](https://support.apple.com/en-us/125666) , you might have to approve an app again if the app makes a significant change (for example, it gets a higher age rating or introduces a new feature).
+## Before you get started
-## Respond to an app exception request
+- [Make sure you have Family Sharing set up](https://setup.icloud.com/family/messages?aaaction=showFamilyInvite&inviteCode=organizer_create&campaign=kbArticle) .
-You can respond to an app exception request on your device, right from the notification or message. If your child is nearby, you can respond directly on their device.

+- [Create a Child Account for your child](https://support.apple.com/102617) , if they don't have one already. Then make sure your child's account is part of your Family Sharing group. It's important that your child has their own Apple Account, and isn't sharing an account with anyone else, like another family member.
-### On your device

+- Update all devices in your Family Sharing group to the latest software version to ensure that your Screen Time settings sync across all the devices in your Family Sharing group. Then [update your parental controls](https://support.apple.com/guide/child-safety/jrzvk3ml3unm) to access the new Screen Time and parental controls.
-When you tap Review the request, the app's page opens. You can approve or decline the exception, or view the app's Age Rating Details.

+## How to allow or block apps on iPhone, iPad, and Mac
-### On your child's device

+In Screen Time, you can see a list of the apps that you've allowed. You can block your child's access to an app at any time. When you block an app, your child can't use it. The app appears dimmed on the Home Screen, but not deleted.

+[Image: iPhone screen showing Marvel Strike Force app with 4m total launch time and options to manage app access.]
+## How to respond to an app exception request

+If your child tries to download an app with an age rating higher than the age restriction that you set for them, they'll see a message that says content restrictions are enabled and they need to ask their parent or guardian for permission. If they ask for an exception, you'll receive a message in the Messages app. You can approve or decline the request right from the message notification or in the Messages app. If you don't approve the request within 24 hours, your child will have to send another request.

+Ask to Buy is on by default for children under 13. * [Depending on your state, country, or region](https://support.apple.com/en-us/125666) , your child might have to request permission to access all apps, regardless of the age rating. If you approved an app, you might have to approve the app again if the app made a significant change (for example, it implemented a higher age rating or introduced a new feature).
+### Respond on your device

+To restore your Apple Watch, you need an iPhone or an iPad. You can use a friend’s device; it doesn’t have to be your iPad or the iPhone that’s paired with your watch. No personal data or information from your watch is shared with the device that you use to restore it.

+- Bring the iPhone or iPad near your watch.

+With Screen Time in visionOS, you can help keep your child's device usage safe, private, and age-appropriate. And Screen Time settings you change on Apple Vision Pro can be shared across your child's other Apple devices.
-You can change or turn off these settings for yourself, or for a child in your Family Sharing group, at any time.

+Apple Vision Pro is designed to fit and be used by individuals 13 years of age and older, and should not be used by children under the age of 13. Children ages 13 years and older should be supervised by an adult while using Apple Vision Pro.
-- In your Apple Vision Pro, open Settings. Tap Screen Time, then tap Content & Privacy Restrictions.

+To use Screen Time and parental controls on Apple Vision Pro, you need to have [Family Sharing set up](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108380) and your child needs their own Apple Account. When you first set up their account, settings are automatically configured based on their age and sync across their iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro, applying wherever relevant. You can customize the settings at any time by following the steps below.
+## Turn Communication Safety on or off

+If your child receives or attempts to send photos or videos that might contain nudity, [Communication Safety](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105069) warns them, blurs the content, and provides helpful resources. For children 13-17, Communication Safety is turned on by default on Apple Vision Pro with the latest software version.

+- Turn Communication Safety on or off.

+## View your recovery heart rate variability (Recovery HRV)
-[Image: An iPhone that shows a graph of heart rate data for the week and an Apple Watch that shows a resting rate of 65 beats per minute.]

+If you have Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, you can view your Recovery HRV. Your Recovery HRV measures how time varies between heartbeats, and can be an indicator of stress and recovery. HRV is sampled while you're still, so the number of measurements you see will vary according to your activity level.

-When you use the Workout app, Apple Watch measures your heart rate continuously during the workout and for 3 minutes after the workout ends to determine a workout recovery rate. If you don't see your heart rate, [check your settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105002) .
+- On your Apple Watch, open the Heart Rate app.

-This information, as well as other data it collects, helps Apple Watch estimate how many calories you’ve burned. In addition, Apple Watch measures your heart rate throughout the day when you’re still, and periodically when you’re walking (Apple Watch Series 1 or later). Since Apple Watch takes these background readings based on your activity, the time between these measurements will vary. Apple Watch also calculates a daily resting rate and walking average by correlating background heart rate readings with accelerometer data when sufficient background readings are available. 1 You can [control which third-party apps have access to your health data from the Health app in Sources](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108779) .
+- Turn the Digital Crown to view your Recovery HRV.
+- Tap info to learn more.

-The optical heart sensor in Apple Watch uses what is known as photoplethysmography. This technology, while difficult to pronounce, is based on a very simple fact: Blood is red because it reflects red light and absorbs green light. Apple Watch uses green LED lights paired with light‑sensitive photodiodes to detect the amount of blood flowing through your wrist at any given moment. When your heart beats, the blood flow in your wrist — and the green light absorption — is greater. Between beats, it’s less. By flashing its LED lights hundreds of times per second, Apple Watch can calculate the number of times the heart beats each minute — your heart rate. The optical heart sensor supports a range of 30–210 beats per minute. In addition, the optical heart sensor is designed to compensate for low signal levels by increasing both LED brightness and sampling rate.

description: Use Siri to help you with the things you need to find, know, or do every day. Find your Apple device here to learn how to use Siri.
diff_excerpt: -- [iPhone](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105020#ios)
+### Identify your version of Siri
-- [iPad](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105020#ipados)
+The features and interactions available to you depend on your device hardware, software version, and settings.
+To find out which version you have, open Settings on your device, then tap or click Siri. In some software versions, Siri preferences are in Settings under Apple Intelligence & Siri.

+- Siri AI (Beta): available for you to [turn on in Settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127893) on [Apple Intelligence-capable devices](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115) in supported languages and regions. When you have Siri AI, the word "beta" appears on the Siri logo in Settings.
+- Siri with Apple Intelligence: the Siri you have when your device uses Apple Intelligence and Siri AI is not enabled. Shown as "Siri Classic" when you have a choice between Siri versions.
+- Siri: for Apple TV, HomePod, and other devices that are not Apple Intelligence-capable; where Apple Intelligence isn't available in your region; or if you have turned off Apple Intelligence.
+On Apple Intelligence-capable models, Apple Watch uses the same version of Siri as its paired iPhone.
+## Talk to Siri
+For most devices, just say Siri or Hey Siri, then immediately say what you need.

+To adjust voice activation for Siri, open Settings on your device, tap or click Siri,* then tap or click Requests. On some versions of iOS and iPadOS, you might need to tap Talk & Type to Siri, Talk to Siri, or Listen for Siri.
+*On some versions of iOS and iPadOS, Siri preferences are in Settings under Apple Intelligence & Siri.
+## Type to Siri
+If you are using Siri AI (Beta), you can always type to Siri.

+- On iPhone or iPad, swipe down from the center of the screen, then type your request in the Search or ask field. You can also type to Siri in the Siri app, or touch and hold an item—text, an image, a document, and more—and tap Ask Siri to open the Search or ask field.

+- On Mac, press Command–Space or click the Siri button in the menu bar to open Spotlight, then type your request. You can also type to Siri in the Siri app, or Control-click an item and choose Ask Siri to type your request directly in the menu.
+For Siri with Apple Intelligence:

+- On iPhone or iPad, turn on [Type to Siri](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/change-siri-accessibility-settings-iphaff1d606/ios) , then double-tap the bottom of the screen and type your request.
+- On a Mac, Type to Siri by clicking the Siri button . On Apple Watch, press and hold the Digital Crown, then type your request.
+If you're not using Apple Intelligence, or if you want to always type your requests instead of speaking them, Type to Siri is an accessibility setting:
+- On iPhone or iPad, open Settings, tap Accessibility, tap Siri, then turn on Type to Siri.
+- On Mac, open System Settings, click Accessibility, click Siri, then turn on Type to Siri.
+- On Apple Watch, press the Digital Crown, open Settings, tap Accessibility, tap Siri, then turn on Type to Siri. Type to Siri isn't currently available with Siri AI on Apple Watch.
+After you turn on Type to Siri, activate Siri with a button, then type your request.
+## Activate Siri with a button
+Instead of saying Siri or Hey Siri, hold down a button or touch the device and speak your request.
+### On iPhone and iPad
+[Image: iPhone with arrow pointing to the Side button to activate Siri.]
+[Image: iPad with arrow pointing to the Top button to activate Siri.]
+Press the side button on iPhone, or the top button on iPad, then make your request. If your device has a Home button, press the Home button instead.

+To turn button activation on or off, open Settings, tap Siri, tap Requests, then turn on Press Side Button for Siri. On some versions of iOS and iPadOS, Siri preferences are in Settings under Apple Intelligence & Siri.
+Find out what to do if [Siri isn't working on your iPhone or iPad](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105037) .
+### On Mac

+On an Apple keyboard with function keys, press and hold the Dictation key or click the Siri button in the menu bar to activate Siri. If you have Siri AI, press Command-Spacebar to open Spotlight, then type your request to Siri.
+[Image: The Siri bar appears after you press the Siri button in the top-right corner of a Mac screen.]
+Find out what to do if [Siri isn't working on your Mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/if-siri-doesnt-work-as-expected-mchl4e4b758d/mac) .
+### On Apple Watch
+Press and hold the Digital Crown, then say what you need.
+To turn Digital Crown activation on or off, open Settings, tap Siri, then tap Press Digital Crown.
+[Image: Apple Watch with arrow pointing to the Digital Crown to activate Siri.]
+Find out what to do if [Siri isn't working on your Watch](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105026) .
title: Use Siri on all your Apple devices
